sources.entry: baRSS – Menu Bar RSS Reader - RSS & Atom feed reader that lives in the system status bar.

summary.one_liner: baRSS is a small open-source macOS menu bar RSS and Atom feed reader that opens articles in your default browser instead of an built-in viewer.
summary.what_it_does: It periodically updates subscribed RSS and Atom feeds and notifies you of new content, with articles listed in a menu bar dropdown. Clicking an article opens it in your browser rather than in an internal content viewer. It reuses ETag and Last-Modified headers to avoid unnecessary downloads, and the author states it stores no cached web sessions or cookies. The README includes a regex converter for turning websites without feeds into feeds, a "show only unread" filter, and Notification Center support in the ToDo list marked as done. Some options, such as menu bar icon and unread dot colors and an OPML backup command, are set through the Terminal with the defaults command.
use_cases: read RSS feeds from the macOS menu bar
get notified of new blog or news posts
follow video channels via feed without an account
keep a feed list backed up as OPML
turn a website without a feed into a feed
how_to_run: Or download a release build from the project's releases page
Build from source: open baRSS/baRSS.xcodeproj in Xcode (requires RSXML2) and build; use Product > Archive for release
stack: RSXML2 (modified fork of Brent Simmons' RSXML) for feed parsing
notable: Opens articles in the default browser, with no built-in content viewer
Reuses ETag and Last-Modified headers to reduce traffic
Built in Objective-C to keep the app around 1 Mb
Regex converter for adding websites that have no RSS feed (expert option)
Hidden option-key shortcuts for marking items read/unread and showing hidden articles
caveats: Requires macOS High Sierra (10.13) or higher
The author warns that the App Store version is counterfeit; the project is distributed via Homebrew or GitHub releases
Several features, such as the regex converter, are described as expert-only or lacking a user-friendly UI
